meta.description: Widely quoted, never sourced. No book, interview or speech has been produced for this Richard Branson line - Wikiquote files it as unsourced.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'I never get the accountants in before I start up a business. It's done on gut feeling, especially if I can see that they are taking the mickey out of the consumer'?
meta.ogDescription: The sentiment is documented. The sentence is not: its trail runs back only to a quote aggregator, and Wikiquote lists it under 'Unsourced'.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: b. 18 July 1950 · founder of the Virgin Group
answer.sourceLine: Every large quote site credits this to Branson, and it matches a view he has put on the record many times. But no book page, interview transcript or speech has ever been produced for this exact wording — the documented trail runs back only to a quote aggregator, and Wikiquote has classed the line as unsourced since 2006.

source.heading: What the trail actually shows

docMeta.dd: Wikiquote article, 15 December 2006 — credited only to thinkexist.com
Unsourced; moved to the talk page on 6 December 2008

source.excerpt: “I never get the accountants in before I start up a business. It’s done on gut feeling, especially if I can see that they are taking the mickey out of the consumer.”
trail: Wikiquote’s Richard Branson page was created on 15 December 2006 with this sentence as its only quote ↗, credited to the quote aggregator thinkexist.com.
Later the same day an editor stripped the aggregator credit and refiled the line under the heading “Unsourced” ↗.
On 6 December 2008 it was moved off the article altogether ↗, into the talk page’s unsourced pile, where it still sits.

The earliest dated appearance is second-hand: in Jeff Burger’s April 2008 Business Jet Traveler interview ↗ the interviewer quotes the line back at Branson — “You’ve said you never get the accountants in before you start a business and that ‘it’s done on gut feeling’” — and Branson answers without correcting the premise. But he is not given as the source of the wording, and his own reply is longer, differently phrased, and mentions taking the mickey out of nobody.
source.excerptNote: The sentence above has never been printed with a source attached. It has been printed with a dateline, though: in April 2008 a Business Jet Traveler interviewer quoted its first two clauses back at Branson — “You’ve said you never get the accountants in before you start a business and that ‘it’s done on gut feeling’” — and he answered at length without disowning it. So the line was in circulation, in a by-lined publication, by 2008. What no source anywhere supplies is where it came from, or any trace at all of the “taking the mickey out of the consumer” clause. That gap is the finding.
source.rightsNote: No work, publication or date can be tied to this wording, so no copyright status can honestly be asserted. If Branson did say it, it was in a modern interview or book, and anything first published from 1931 onward is presumed in copyright in the United States to its author or publisher — so this line should not be treated as public domain.

author.heading: Richard Branson
author.metaLine: b. 1950 · English business magnate, founder of the Virgin Group
author.bio: Sir Richard Charles Nicholas Branson, born 18 July 1950, co-founded the Virgin Group in 1970 and grew it into a conglomerate spanning record shops, airlines and spaceflight, launching Virgin Atlantic in 1984 and taking a knighthood in 2000 for services to entrepreneurship. He is also one of the most-quoted living businesspeople, and his taste for a blunt, funny, anti-establishment one-liner is exactly why so many sentences circulate under his name with nothing behind them.

misattribution.heading: The problem is the source, not the name
misattribution.intro: This is not a case of the wrong person’s name on a quote. It is a case of no source underneath one — and of a documented Branson remark being quietly displaced by a snappier sentence nobody can date.

items.who: Quote aggregators — thinkexist.com, and after it BrainyQuote, AZQuotes, QuoteFancy
items.why: Wikiquote’s Branson page was created on 15 December 2006 with this line as its only quote ↗, credited to thinkexist.com. Later that day an editor refiled it under the heading “Unsourced” ↗. No aggregator since has supplied a date, a publication or a transcript.

In an April 2008 Business Jet Traveler interview ↗ the interviewer opens by quoting the line back at him — “You’ve said you never get the accountants in before you start a business and that ‘it’s done on gut feeling’” — and Branson answers without correcting it. That is the strongest evidence the attribution has, and it is still second-hand: the journalist gives no source, and Branson’s own words in reply are longer, differently phrased, and say nothing about taking the mickey out of the consumer.

Readers routinely assume the line comes from the autobiography. That has never been demonstrated: no citation anywhere gives a page number, and the Internet Archive copy ↗ is lending-restricted, so we could not check it either.

misattribution.truthLine: No source has ever been produced. The live Wikiquote page ↗ sources Branson to the BBC, The Guardian and the Sunday Mirror; this line is not on it. It sits on the talk page under “Unsourced” ↗, and Quote Investigator has no article on it ↗.

context.heading: The idea is his. The sentence is unclaimed.
lead: The sentiment is not in doubt. Branson has said versions of it for decades: that he trusts instinct over spreadsheets, and that the industries worth attacking are the ones whose incumbents have got comfortable at the customer’s expense. Asked in Business Jet Traveler how he decided to start an airline ↗, he described the miserable flights he had endured on other carriers, then added that if he had gotten the accountants in, “they would have almost definitely told me all the reasons why it wasn’t going to work.”

What is in doubt is the sentence. The popular wording is tighter and funnier than anything we could find him saying in a documented interview, and it arrives everywhere with no dateline attached. Its paper trail begins on a quote aggregator rather than in a transcript — the pattern you see when a line has been tidied in circulation instead of copied from a source.
context.detailsSummary: What we checked, and what we could not
detailsBody: “Taking the mickey” is British slang for mocking or sending someone up, and it is genuinely part of Branson’s vocabulary: in a 2006 Wine Spectator interview ↗ about Virgin Vines he said Virgin “felt someone needed to take the mickey out of the whole wine-snobbery thing.” The disputed line leans on a looser second sense — taking liberties with someone — which is how the phrase has to read when the target is a consumer rather than a bit of snobbery. Either way the idiom is no argument against him, and no evidence for this particular sentence either.

We could not read inside the 1998 autobiography ↗, because the Internet Archive copy is lending-restricted, so the book cannot be ruled out. What can be said is that the version of Branson’s decision-making philosophy that reference works quote from Losing My Virginity is a different sentence: “I rely far more on gut instinct than researching huge amounts of statistics.” ↗
context.pull: If I had gotten the accountants in, they would have almost definitely told me all the reasons why it wasn’t going to work.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's Talk:Richard Branson page lists this quote verbatim under the heading "Unsourced", alongside other unsourced Branson lines.
The Talk:Richard Branson revision history shows the page was created on 6 December 2008 by InvisibleSun with the edit summary "Transferred unsourced quotes to talk page."
The first revision of Wikiquote's Richard Branson article, 15 December 2006 at 20:52, consists of this quote alone, credited to "(thinkexist.com)".
The next revision the same day, 15 December 2006 at 22:42, places the quote under the section heading "Unsourced" and drops the thinkexist.com credit.

The current Wikiquote Richard Branson article does not contain this quote; its listed quotes are sourced to outlets including a BBC interview (21 February 2009), The Guardian (20 September 2008) and the Sunday Mirror (16 January 2000).

Business Jet Traveler's April 2008 interview by Jeff Burger, conducted at Branson's New York offices, quotes him saying "If I had gotten the accountants in, they would have almost definitely told me all the reasons why it wasn't going to work" — and contains no passage about "taking the mickey out of the consumer".
A Quote Investigator site search for "Branson accountants" returns "Nothing Found" — QI has no article on this quotation.
Losing My Virginity: The Autobiography by Richard Branson was published by Virgin Publishing, London, in 1998; the Internet Archive copy is lending-restricted rather than fully readable.
Encyclopedia.com's Richard Branson entry quotes from his 1998 autobiography Losing My Virginity: "I rely far more on gut instinct than researching huge amounts of statistics."

Wikipedia states Sir Richard Charles Nicholas Branson was born 18 July 1950, co-founded the Virgin Group in 1970, founded Virgin Atlantic in 1984, and was knighted on 30 March 2000 for services to entrepreneurship.

Wine Spectator's "Wine Talk: Richard Branson" (Julie Mautner, 7 August 2006) quotes Branson: "Virgin is a playful brand and we felt someone needed to take the mickey out of the whole wine-snobbery thing."
